title: Four requests, four ways in
scenario:
You run the design team at a stationery brand. Four requests reach you in one week. Each one needs some code, and you must say where it should live: a plugin, an app inside Canva, an MCP server or a REST API script.

Use the exhibit. API names, surfaces and rules are from Figma's and Canva's docs. The brand, the people and the requests are made up for this case.
exhibit:
REQUEST 1 (made up), from the brand lead
  "Every night, check all 300 Figma files for raw hex colours, and
   email me a list in the morning. Nobody will be online."

REQUEST 2 (made up), from marketing
  "Our team writes briefs in an AI assistant. We want to say 'make
   five Canva posts from this brief' right there."

REQUEST 3 (made up), from a designer
  A Figma plugin that swaps placeholder photos for photos from the
  brand library at assets.example.com. First test: every network call
  is blocked with a CSP error. The manifest has no networkAccess entry.

REQUEST 4 (made up), from a developer
  A public Canva app for the Apps Marketplace. One feature uses an
  API that Canva marks as a preview.

DOC LINES (from the docs)
  Figma plugins: "It's not possible to build plugins that run in the background."
  Figma REST API: "Figma does not need to be open and a user does not need to be present."
  Canva: "The Canva Apps SDK, Connect APIs, and MCP are now unified in the Canva Developers SDK."

questions.prompt: Where should the nightly check in request 1 live?

options.text: A Figma plugin, set to start by itself each night and run through all 300 files
options.explanation: Figma says plugins can't run in the background, and a plugin reads only the open file.

options.text: A widget on each file's canvas, which checks the colours whenever it is refreshed
options.explanation: A widget acts only on the file where it's inserted, and someone has to open it.

options.text: A REST API script on a schedule, since Figma need not be open and nobody need be there
options.explanation: Right. Figma's comparison page names scheduled scripts as the REST API's model, and it can read many files.

options.text: A Dev Mode plugin, because Dev Mode plugins are allowed to run while nobody is there
options.explanation: Figma says Dev Mode plugins are read-only. No page says they run in the background.

questions.prompt: Which Canva surface fits request 2 best?

options.text: Apps inside Canva, because the app runs in an iframe in the side panel of the editor
options.explanation: That surface reaches users while they design in Canva. Marketing works in an AI assistant.

options.text: Canva for AI assistants, because users can create designs by asking in their AI tools
options.explanation: Right. This surface connects to the Canva MCP server, so users ask in the AI tools they already use.

options.text: Canva for your platform, because the REST APIs are the only way an AI can reach Canva
options.explanation: Canva also offers an MCP server for AI assistants. REST is for your own platform.

options.text: The Connect APIs plugin, which Canva now lists as its own fourth product for AI work
options.explanation: Canva says the Connect APIs are now the Canva REST APIs. There is no fourth product.

questions.prompt: In request 3, every network call is blocked. What should the designer's developer fix first?

options.text: Add networkAccess to the manifest, with assets.example.com in allowedDomains
options.explanation: Right. Figma says to list the domains your plugin calls under allowedDomains in networkAccess.

options.text: Move all of the code into Dev Mode, since only Dev Mode plugins may use a network
options.explanation: Figma's plugin pages list network calls for normal plugins too. Dev Mode is read-only.

options.text: Run the plugin twice at the same time, so one copy loads and the other one edits
options.explanation: Figma says users can only run one plugin and one action at a time.

options.text: Turn the plugin into a widget, because widgets have no rules for network requests
options.explanation: No page says this. The CSP error points to the plugin's own network list.

questions.prompt: What will happen to request 4 as it is planned now?

options.text: It ships at once, because preview APIs are Canva's newest and most stable features
options.explanation: Canva says preview APIs may change without notice and are not for production.

options.text: It ships, but Canva marks the app as a preview app in the marketplace for a year
options.explanation: No page describes this. Canva says such an app will not pass review.

options.text: It ships once the team adds a second intent, which unlocks the preview features
options.explanation: Intents decide where Canva shows an app. They do not unlock preview APIs.

options.text: It fails review, because public apps that use preview APIs will not pass the review
options.explanation: Right. Canva says public apps that use preview APIs or features will not pass the review process.
